subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "account"
reading: A reading: the accounts the platforms name are the seller's accounts with the party that processes and holds its funds, which CM-PAY-004 holds (Shopify's Payment Processor Accounts and Global-e account, WooCommerce's Stripe Express account and Stripe's pooled accounts, BigCommerce's PayPal platform account that handles settlement, the provider's merchant account behind Zid Payments' interface for providers), and, where the seller takes payments through another gateway, its own account there, which CM-PAY-011 holds (Salla's gateway account and Al Rajhi Mokafaa, Zid's Tap, BigCommerce's Stripe and Braintree accounts). The instalment providers' accounts (Tabby, Tamara, MIS Pay, Madfu, Emkan) are CM-PAY-015's, and Zid Pay's account balance CM-PAY-005's (notes).

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "licensed"
reading: A reading: the licence the question asks for is that of the entity that processes, acquires and holds the funds behind the payment service, which CM-PAY-004 holds with each entity's scope (Shopify's Payment Facilitator entities and Acquirer per Designated Country, Stripe's authorised entities for WooCommerce); Zid answers for Tap, a third-party gateway licensed by the central bank, which is CM-PAY-011's (ZD-C-011/responsible/ZD-S-0611).

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "terms of service"
reading: A reading: the terms that bind the seller are of two kinds the model holds apart: the processor's or provider's own terms behind the payment service (Shopify's Payment Processor Terms and Pass-Through Terms, Stripe's Connected Account Agreement, Salla's payment services contract), which CM-PAY-004 holds, and the platform company's own agreement for the service, with its contracting entity and law (Zid Pay's terms with Zid's company, WooCommerce, Inc. or WooCommerce Ireland Ltd., the Shopify entity for the Designated Country, Salla's usage agreement), which CM-ACC-002 holds.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "payout schedule"
reading: A reading: the schedule is the payment service's payout of the seller's balance to its bank account, CM-PAY-005 (Shopify's daily, weekly or monthly payouts, Salla's transfer cycle by plan, WooPayments' payout schedule, Zid Pay's deposit days, BigCommerce Payments' payout frequency); Salla and Zid also give the schedule of cash on delivery remitted by their shipping services (CM-PAY-029) and of withdrawals from the store wallet (CM-PLN-006), so those capabilities carry it too.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "payout timing"
reading: A reading: the timing is the delay between the buyer's payment and the payout reaching the seller's bank, which the payment service's payouts carry, CM-PAY-005 (Shopify's settlement times by country and risk, Salla's processing and settlement stage, WooPayments' pending period, BigCommerce Payments' Fast and Standard payouts); Zid's answers also time the transfer from its wallet (CM-PLN-006) and the remittance of cash on delivery to the wallet (CM-PAY-029).

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "Minimum payout amount"
reading: A reading: the minimum is a condition on the payment service's payout of the seller's balance, CM-PAY-005, whose cells already hold it as stated (Salla's 100 riyals, 250 dirhams and one dinar, Zid's 100 riyals, one dinar and Mazeed's 500 riyals, Shopify's minimum in certain countries); WooPayments' minimum balance per payout currency and minimum instant payout are the same thing.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "reserve"
reading: A reading: a reserve is funds the payment service, or the processor behind it, holds back from the seller's payouts for a time, which is CM-PAY-006's thing by its name and cells (Shopify's reserves and its processors' Rolling Reserve and Reserve, Stripe's fixed and rolling reserves for WooPayments, Zid Pay's reserve amount); BigCommerce's only statement is PayPal's minimum account reserve, which a BigCommerce setting lowers (notes).

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "held"
reading: A reading: funds held are funds kept from the seller's payout, CM-PAY-006 (payout holds and reserves); the model also cites payouts paused or held for the payout account (Shopify's pause on a new payout destination, WooPayments' balance held until a bank account is added, its paused and suspended payouts) in CM-PAY-005, so the point lands on both, CM-PAY-006 first.
conflict: count (rows: S01-VP-18, model): Salla. The subject's S01-SA-160 ('Store verification is required to complete transfers. Unverified stores will have funds pending until verification is complete', scope Saudi Arabia), S01-SA-161 (verification required for transferring the electronic payments balance) and S01-SA-135 ('يتم تعليق عمليات الدفع والسداد إلى أن يتم إتمام خطوات توثيق المتجر', KSA) state Salla's own payment service holding the seller's funds back from transfer, its built-in behaviour, which B-extent's rule places core; CM-PAY-006's Salla cell holds nothing (none-held, its search included معلق and تعليق التحويل), and CM-PAY-005's Salla cell cites only the bank-account name match as shows (SA-C-112/decides/SA-S-0098). A reading: the statements bear out core on CM-PAY-006 for Salla; S01-SA-089 (the Saudi Central Bank's and the Ministry's restrictions may delay transfers) is a term of Salla's agreement and supports no placement | count (rows: S01-VP-18, model): BigCommerce. The subject's S01-BC-082 ('For new BigCommerce Payments accounts, initial payments are held for up to 21 days before being available for payout', pointing to PayPal's page on payments on hold) and S01-BC-083 ('Funds may be held or blocked for several reasons ... Check the Actions section ... complete any requests for documents or verification') state a hold on BigCommerce Payments, the platform's own service (core in CM-PAY-002, BC-C-025/reason/BC-S-0149), which reads as core by its built-in behaviour; CM-PAY-006's BigCommerce cell holds nothing (searched hold, held). A reading: the pointer to PayPal's page may mean PayPal places the hold, which would be outside, not core; either way the cell holds nothing. What would settle it: the PayPal page S01-BC-082 cites, or BigCommerce Payments' terms, naming who places the hold
outcome: model amended: C-anchor/evidence.tsv CM-PAY-006 salla, core on S01-SA-160, S01-SA-135 and S01-SA-161: Salla's payment service holds an unverified store's funds; the class's count up by one (the coordinator) | model amended: C-bigcommerce/evidence.tsv CM-PAY-006 bigcommerce, shows on S01-BC-082 and S01-BC-083: the hold on new BigCommerce Payments accounts is stated, not who holds, so no count changes; PayPal's page on new accounts' holds, or BigCommerce Payments' terms, would settle who (the coordinator)

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "deducted"
reading: A reading: what is deducted is taken from the seller's balance before or at payout, CM-PAY-005 (refunds, chargebacks, reserves and set-off netted from Shopify's, WooPayments' and Zid Pay's payouts); the platforms answer what is deducted in three more capabilities: the payment service's own processing fees (CM-PAY-007), the platform's own charges collected from the seller's balance (Salla's waybills and dues from the wallet or e-payments, Zid's dues from wallet deposits, CM-PLN-005), and financing repaid from a share of sales (Salla's 25 per cent, Stripe Capital's repayment rate, Zid's financing, CM-PAY-026).

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "Termination"
reading: A reading: the question is what becomes of the seller's funds when the payment service ends: the balance paid out or settled (Shopify's funds in the Financial Services Provider's custody paid out, Zid's balance transferred to the bank when Zid Pay is turned off, Salla's pending e-payments returned to consumers), CM-PAY-005, or held on after it (Shopify's processor holding funds, the reserve provisions that survive, Zid's reserve settled at closing and Mazeed's held funds), CM-PAY-006.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "refunded to your customers"
reading: A reading: funds refunded to the buyers are funds the payment service holds back from the seller's payout and returns to their source instead, CM-PAY-006 (Shopify's funds held or refunded where the seller does not pass its checks, Zid Pay's holds ending in a return to the source, ZD-C-037/responsible/ZD-S-0772); where the return is a sanction for a breach of the platform's rules (Salla's Article Ten, WooCommerce's prohibited uses), it is also the platform's enforcement, CM-TRU-009, which cites the same Zid statement.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "pay in installments"
basis: SH-C-075/boundary/SH-S-0317;concern:SH-C-075;term:Shop Pay Installments;term:buy now, pay later;term:الدفع الآجل
reading: A reading: paying in instalments is CM-PAY-015's thing by its name and cells; the point asks when and by whom the seller is paid under it, which each platform answers in that capability's terms (Shopify pays in full after capture, WooPayments receives the whole amount, Tabby and Tamara pay Salla's merchants, BigCommerce's merchants are paid up front while the shopper owes PayPal).
conflict: placement (rows: S01-D13, model): Salla. CM-PAY-015's Salla cell is core only (SA-C-118/where/SA-S-0070, SA-C-118/decides/SA-S-1965 and the released flags SA-C-118/decides/SA-S-3125, SA-S-3128), and its reading says who lends isn't stated; Tabby and Tamara are slot fillers on it but placed nowhere. The subject's S01-SA-102 (Tabby transfers to the store first and collects from the customers later), S01-SA-104 (all payments settled by Tamara on the schedule agreed with the store) and S01-SA-101 (payments through Tabby are collected through Tabby, not Salla Payments, with transfer times and fees under the merchant's agreement with Tabby, UAE) show third parties doing the instalment financing and its settlement. A reading: the statements bear out outside beside core for Salla | count (rows: S01-D13, model): BigCommerce. CM-PAY-015's BigCommerce cell is not-stated (BC-C-027/where/BC-S-0161, BC-C-025/where/BC-S-0142, BC-I-0438, BC-I-0442, BC-I-0445, all shows), its reading saying no statement names instalments or buy now, pay later. The subject's S01-BC-024 (BigCommerce's own page bigcommerce.com/payments/paypal/, under 'Help drive sales with Pay Later': 'Allow customers to pay in installments with Pay in 4 and Pay Monthly while you get paid up front') and S01-BC-022 (BigCommerce's product page Consumer financing: 'Our consumer financing integrations guarantee you get paid') name instalments as the platform's own product line, which the model's convention for a product line (as in CM-RET-001's BigCommerce cell) places core; S01-BC-094 (PayPal Pay Later: the shopper owes the money to PayPal) shows PayPal doing the lending, outside. A reading: the statements bear out core with outside (PayPal) for BigCommerce; what would settle it is whether a marketing product page's line counts as a product line in B-extent's sense
outcome: model amended: C-anchor/evidence.tsv CM-PAY-015 salla, outside on S01-SA-101, S01-SA-102 and S01-SA-104: Tabby and Tamara finance and collect (the coordinator) | model amended: C-bigcommerce/evidence.tsv CM-PAY-015 bigcommerce, outside on S01-BC-094 and S01-BC-024 (PayPal) and extension-point on S01-BC-022 (the financing integrations): no statement places it in BigCommerce's own core, so the count doesn't change (the coordinator)

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "currency"
reading: A reading: the point asks which currency the seller's funds settle and pay out in, a value every amount carries, so its reach is the cross-cutting decision on money records and currency; the main capability is the payout, CM-PAY-005 (Salla's dirham and dinar payout accounts and riyal receipts, Shopify's and WooPayments' payout currencies per country), with the conversion when the payment's currency differs (WooPayments, BigCommerce, CM-MKS-007) and the wallet currencies Zid won't let the seller withdraw (CM-PLN-006).
